hospitals.peds_trauma_level: Level I pediatric trauma center (ACS verified)
hospitals.description: Boston Children's is a freestanding, Harvard-affiliated pediatric academic center in the Longwood Medical Area and the largest pediatric hospital in New England. It runs a regional PICU along with cardiac and medical-surgical ICUs, an AAP-verified Level IV NICU, and an ACS Level I pediatric trauma program. The hospital is known for quaternary subspecialty care, a huge research enterprise, and fetal and complex care programs that draw patients from around the world. It also staffs pediatric units and nurseries at several community hospitals across eastern Massachusetts, so NP roles exist both on the Longwood campus and in the network. The campus sits in a dense medical district that is reachable by the Green Line and commuter rail.
highlights: Ranked number 1 on the U.S. News Best Children's Hospitals Honor Roll for 2024-25 (tenth straight year)
485 licensed beds
AAP-verified Level IV NICU
ACS Level I pediatric trauma center
Regional PICU plus cardiac and medical-surgical ICUs
Harvard Medical School primary pediatric teaching hospital
Network of community hospital pediatric programs across Massachusetts
hospitals.notes: Very large NP workforce, with frequent postings for inpatient medicine, ICU (PICU, CICU, MSICU), float pool and subspecialty NP or PA roles. Boston Children's also staffs pediatric inpatient units and nurseries at community hospitals (South Shore, Winchester, Cape Cod, St. Luke's New Bedford and others), and those roles are posted on the Boston Children's board. Acquired Franciscan Children's in 2023.

hospitals.description: Mass General for Children is the pediatric hospital inside Massachusetts General Hospital on the Charles River edge of downtown Boston, and the only children's hospital in the Mass General Brigham network. It holds about 100 pediatric beds, including a 14-bed mixed medical-surgical PICU for patients up to age 21. Its NICU is described as Level IV in Harvard med-peds materials, while an older Wikipedia figure lists Level III with 18 bassinets. MGH carries Level I adult and pediatric trauma verification. The hospital is a major Harvard teaching site, and the pediatric program also supports affiliated community units such as Newton-Wellesley.

hospitals.description: Shriners Children's Boston is a pediatric burn and reconstructive surgery hospital on Blossom Street, next to Massachusetts General Hospital. It treats acute burns, burn scars and reconstruction, cleft lip and palate, and orthopaedic conditions, and families pay nothing out of pocket. In 2020 it cut licensed inpatient beds from 30 to 9 (4 burn and 5 pediatric) and closed one of three operating rooms, moving toward a mostly outpatient and surgical model. It keeps close clinical and research ties with MGH.
highlights: Pediatric burn center next to MGH
Licensed beds reduced from 30 to 9 in 2020 (4 burn, 5 pediatric)
Burn, reconstructive, cleft and orthopaedic surgery
Care provided regardless of ability to pay
hospitals.notes: Small inpatient census. NP roles here are typically burn or surgical APPs. Careers URL is a placeholder for the national Shriners site and should be verified. Within about 150 m of MGH (different institution).

hospitals.description: UMass Memorial Children's Medical Center is the pediatric hospital within UMass Memorial Medical Center in Worcester and the only children's hospital in central Massachusetts. It draws referrals from central Massachusetts, northern Connecticut and southern New Hampshire. The University Campus houses a 30-bed general pediatric ward, the region's only PICU (10 beds) and a pediatric emergency department. The NICU, listed at 49 beds and Level III, sits about a mile away at the Memorial Campus, which is the regional perinatal center with 24/7 neonatologist coverage. The medical center holds ACS Level I verification for both adults and children and is the clinical partner of UMass Chan Medical School.
highlights: Only children's hospital and only PICU in central Massachusetts
Level I adult and pediatric trauma center
10-bed PICU and 30-bed general pediatric ward
Level III NICU (about 49 beds) at the Memorial Campus regional perinatal center
UMass Chan Medical School teaching hospital
Over 200 pediatric clinicians across 30+ specialties
hospitals.notes: Two Worcester campuses: pediatric floor, PICU and peds ED at University Campus (55 Lake Ave N); NICU at Memorial Campus (119 Belmont St). One record covers both. Worcester is about 45 to 60 minutes west of Boston with lower housing costs.

hospitals.description: Baystate Children's Hospital is the pediatric hospital within Baystate Medical Center in Springfield and the only children's hospital in western Massachusetts. It has about 107 beds and runs the region's only PICU and NICU. The Level III NICU has 55 beds (33 acute and 22 step-down) and is staffed by neonatologists and about ten neonatal advanced practice providers, supporting more than 4,000 deliveries a year. The Sadowsky Family Pediatric Emergency Department has 18 rooms and is staffed by board-certified pediatric emergency physicians. Baystate is the Level I adult and Level II pediatric trauma center for the Pioneer Valley and is the western campus of UMass Chan Medical School.
highlights: Only children's hospital, PICU and NICU in western Massachusetts
55-bed Level III NICU with about 10 neonatal APPs

hospitals.description: Cape Cod Hospital in Hyannis is the 283-bed referral hospital for Cape Cod and the Islands and the flagship of Cape Cod Healthcare. Since July 2021 Boston Children's physicians have run its pediatric program around the clock, covering the inpatient pediatric unit, the newborn nursery and labor and delivery, and consulting in the emergency department, with video support for transferring critically ill newborns. Maternity and pediatric inpatient care for the Cape was consolidated here when Falmouth Hospital stopped births and pediatric admissions in 2020. The hospital gained Level III adult trauma designation in January 2025. It is a seasonal resort area with a year-round population and a long drive to Boston.

Children admitted from Charlton Memorial and Tobey hospitals come here. Boston Children's physicians work on site through a clinical collaboration that lets them consult the Longwood campus in real time. The hospital also holds Level II adult trauma designation.

hospitals.description: Women & Infants is Rhode Island's dedicated obstetric and newborn hospital, next to Rhode Island Hospital and Hasbro Children's in Providence's hospital district. It delivers about 8,400 babies a year, among the most in the country, and its NICU is an 80-bed Level III unit. The NICU moved into a five-story South Pavilion in 2009 that earned LEED Gold. It is the primary Brown teaching hospital for obstetrics, gynecology and newborn pediatrics, and its Brown neonatology group also covers nurseries at Kent Hospital and Sturdy Memorial. A new Brown University Labor and Delivery Center with 20 rooms opened in March 2025.

hospitals.description: Connecticut Children's is the state's freestanding children's hospital, on Washington Street in Hartford right next to Hartford Hospital. Wikipedia gives it 185 to 230 beds and ACS Level I pediatric trauma verification, one of two Level I pediatric trauma centers in Connecticut. It runs a PICU, a pediatric emergency department and neonatal intensive care. The neonatology directory credits the Level IV NICU housed at Hartford Hospital to the Connecticut Children's program, and its neonatologists also staff the UConn John Dempsey NICU. It is the main pediatric teaching hospital for UConn and Quinnipiac and has specialty sites in Farmington, Glastonbury, Shelton and Waterbury. Hartford is about 30 minutes from Springfield, MA and two hours from Boston or New York.

hospitals.description: Yale New Haven Children's Hospital is the 202-bed pediatric hospital inside Yale New Haven Hospital's York Street campus. It is Connecticut's top-ranked children's hospital and the main pediatric teaching site for Yale School of Medicine. It runs a 19-bed PICU, an AAP-verified Level IV NICU on two floors (68 beds per a neonatology directory) with a dedicated neonatal MRI and couplet rooms, a Level I pediatric trauma program, and the region's first inpatient child and adolescent psychiatric unit. Its physicians also staff the dedicated pediatric ED at Greenwich Hospital and pediatric services across the Yale New Haven Health system. The campus is in downtown New Haven near the Yale campus and Metro-North to New York.
